olivia: Quick design note — compare lightweight admit tokens vs per-request reservation slots for retry fast-paths.
noah: Token wins on memory footprint. Reservation slots simpler to reason about capacity.
kevin: Tokens: TTL 50-200ms, issued on accept, redeemed by retry. Reservations: allocate N slots/route and hold for TTL.
li: Streaming corner case: both avoid replay. Token redemption should only select replica/fallback variant, not replay stream.
dana: Billing: prefer bill-on-consume. Metrics: token_issued/redeemed/expired and slot_acquired/used/preempted.
olivia: Safety: cluster-wide token budget + per-tenant rate limit to prevent storms.
noah: Preemption: if a holder stalls, auto-expire on progress staleness (bytes/frame heartbeat).
kevin: Config snippet idea: ```yaml
routes:
  - name: completions
    admit_token: { enabled: true, ttl_ms: 150, max_per_100ms: 200 }
```
li: Security: internal-only header X-Internal-Admit, strip at egress; require mTLS.
dana: Perf test: chaos upstream flaps (30% replicas, 100-500ms outages). Measure p50/p95/p99 for new requests and retries for token vs slot vs baseline.
deploy-bot: feature-flag rollout started for admit-token on canary at 1748901255 :rocket: 
olivia: Next step: short RFC draft with tradeoffs, failure modes table, and simulation results. I'll drop draft here.
